newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican peso weaker on U.S. job data worries.
newsitem.headline: Mexican peso weaker on U.S. job data worries.

text.p: The Mexican peso opened generally weaker on Wednesday due to nervousness ahead of U.S. employment data due at the end of the week, dealers said.
Dealers said the peso was affected by a small rebound in the U.S. long bond yield and fears it will rise further if U.S. job data due on Friday appears inflationary.
"I think the market is taking dollar positions on the expectation there will be a technical adjustment in the exchange rate," one dealer told Reuters.

The same-day peso shed 2.20 centavos to 7.9250/7.9280 per dollar after the first hour of trading, while 24- and 48-hour contracts slipped 1.2 and 1.1 centavos to 7.9280/7.9310 and 7.9310/7.9340, respectively.
